title: One-coordinate supported vanishing on the full tame root tower
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its norm topology, and an algebraic closure $\Omega\supset E$ with its extended norm topology. For $F=E$ or $\Omega$, let $C_F(Q)=C(Q,F)$ on all profinite sets, using all continuous functions [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and put $C_{F,X}=p_X^*C_F$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Work with internal modules, ordinary unbounded derived categories and K-injective total right derived direct images on small pro-etale sites [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Lisse means pro-etale locally finite free [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. All sites, parameter sets and resolutions lie in compatible coefficient universes.

Let $Y$ be a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $V\to Y$ an affine etale chart with reduced strict normal crossings boundary cut out by $t_1\cdots t_r$, whose branches are precisely $V(t_a)$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to V$ be affine pro-etale. Set
$$T=\operatorname{Spec}\left(\varinjlim_{(n,p)=1}R[x_{a,n}]_{1\leq a\leq r}/(x_{a,n}^n-t_a)_a\right),$$
where positive $n$ are ordered by divisibility and $x_{a,n}\mapsto x_{a,m}^{m/n}$ for $n\mid m$. For $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ let $T_J=T[1/\prod_{b\in J}t_b]$.
Let $a\notin J$ and let $d_{a,J}:D_{a,J}\hookrightarrow T_J$ be the closed subscheme cut out by $t_a$. The complementary open is $T_{J\cup\{a\}}$, a principal affine open. For any finite-rank lisse $C_{F,T}$-module $\mathcal N$, one has
$$R\underline\Gamma_{D_{a,J}}(\mathcal N|_{T_J}[0])=0$$
in $D(D_{a,J},C_F)$. Here $\underline\Gamma_D(\mathcal H)=d^*\ker(\mathcal H\to e_*e^*\mathcal H)$ for the closed inclusion $d$ and complementary open inclusion $e$; its right derived functor is [det-lem-formal-closed-support-adjunction]. This includes an empty $D_{a,J}$ and rank zero; for $r=0$ there is no pair $(J,a)$. No direct image to $U$, no stratum identification, and no profinite-parameter or group-invariants comparison is asserted.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-formulated input: vanishing with support on one branch after adjoining all prime-to-p roots, also after inverting other branches. Exact all-continuous reference WANTED; this statement is not quoted as a theorem of the blueprint.

proof.text:
Write $B=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ and first form the tower over $V$ itself. Fix $J,a$ as in the statement and set
$$B_n=B[x_{1,n},\ldots,x_{r,n}]/(x_{b,n}^n-t_b)_b,\quad X_n=\operatorname{Spec}(B_n[1/\prod_{b\in J}t_b]).$$
The index is the positive integers prime to $p$, ordered by divisibility, with least element $1$. For $n\mid m$, put $e=m/n$. As a $B_n$-algebra, $B_m$ is obtained by adjoining $y_b$ satisfying $y_b^e=x_{b,n}$; eliminate the old variables to check this presentation. Repeated monic division [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] gives the basis $\prod_b y_b^{d_b}$, $0\leq d_b<e$, so the transition is finite free, also after the indicated localization; in the same way $B_n$ is free over $B$. Since $n$ is prime to $p$ it is a unit in the $k$-algebra $B$, so $B_n$ is regular [lem-sfb-snc-finite-root-regular-ring], and so is its localization $X_n$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-regular-ring]. The ring of $D_n=V(x_{a,n})$ is the same localization of $B_n/(x_{a,n})$, which is regular by the face $J=\{a\}$ of [lem-sfb-snc-finite-root-face-regular]; hence $D_n$ is regular. The intersections $V(t_a,t_b)$ may be reducible or empty, so the root-ring lemma is not applied to $V(t_a)$ directly. The boundary ideal $(t_1\cdots t_r)$ is effective Cartier [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], so the product, and hence its factor $t_a$, is a nonzerodivisor on $B$. By freeness $t_a$ stays a nonzerodivisor on $B_n$ and after localization, and so does $x_{a,n}$, which divides $t_a=x_{a,n}^n$. Thus $D_n$ is regular Cartier. The empty divisor case causes no exception.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: the finite root stages and their regular coordinate divisors

proof.text:
Fix $s\geq1$ and $A_s=\mathbf Z/\ell^s\mathbf Z$. On $X_n$ let $j_n:X_n-D_n\hookrightarrow X_n$ and put $K_n=\operatorname{fib}(A_{s,X_n}	o Rj_{n,*}A_s)$. The finite supported Cartier purity statement [lem-sfb-ramified-cartier-supported-purity] identifies $K_n$ with $i_{n,*}A_{s,D_n}(-1)[-2]$. All schemes here are regular Noetherian affines, the immersion has codimension one, and $\ell$ is invertible since $\ell
e p$. In particular $H^qK_n=0$ for $q
e2$. The generator of $D_n$ pulls back to $x_{a,m}^{m/n}$. Apply [lem-sfb-ramified-cartier-supported-purity] with $f=x_{a,n}$ and $g=x_{a,m}$: the transition on $H^2K_n$ is exactly $m/n$ times the Tate-line exchange. There is no assertion that the scheme-theoretic pullback $V(x_{a,m}^{m/n})$ equals the reduced divisor $D_m$. For $m=n\ell^s$ that transition is zero. This $m$ is an allowed index because $p
e\ell$.

source.place: The supported finite-stage purity class and its ramification factor

proof.text: Let $X=\varprojlim_n X_n$ and $W=X[1/t_a]$, with $j:W\hookrightarrow X$. The opens $X_n-D_n=X_n[1/t_a]$ form an inverse system with affine transitions and limit $W$. Apply [lem-kun-0eym] to these principal open immersions, with the constant sheaves $A_s$ and identity coefficient transitions. It identifies all $R^qj_*$ with the filtered colimits of the pulled-back finite-stage higher images, with precisely the exchange maps used in step 2. The same assertion for the identity maps identifies the constant sheaves. Taking the long exact sequences of the fibres and using exactness of filtered colimits of sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaves-filtered-colimits-exact] therefore computes every cohomology sheaf of $\operatorname{fib}(A_{s,X}\to Rj_*A_s)$ as the colimit of the pulled-back $H^qK_n$. All these colimits are zero: only degree two can occur, and every degree-two section is killed at $n\ell^s$. Consequently the actual unit $A_{s,X}[0]\to Rj_*j^*A_{s,X}[0]$ is an isomorphism in the etale derived category, for every $s$.

source.place: Tag 0EYM (lemma-relative-colimit-general): continuity for the principal opens and their actual units

proof.text: Apply [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] to the quasi-compact quasi-separated principal open $j$ and the bounded-below etale object $A_s[0]$. Its comparison is compatible with the adjunction unit. Thus the unit just proved invertible pulls to the actual unit $A_{s,X}[0]\to Rj_*j^*A_{s,X}[0]$ on the pro-etale site. This passage concerns the discrete finite ring $A_s$ only. It holds for this possibly non-Noetherian limit $X$, since the comparison node assumes arbitrary schemes and only requires $j$ to be qcqs.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: the finite discrete comparison before changing the topology of the coefficients

proof.text:
The inverse system $(X_n)$ satisfies [lem-sfb-torsion-acyclic-norm-coefficient-test]: its schemes are regular affine and finite type over $k$, its transitions are finite locally free by step 1, and $f_0=t_a$ is a nonzerodivisor at every stage. Step 4 supplies the finite-torsion open-unit hypothesis at its limit for every $s\geq1$. Base change of $U\to V$ along $X\to V$ gives an affine pro-etale map $X'=X\times_VU\to X$ by [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability]. The presentations identify $X'$ with the $T_J$ of the item, and $W\times_X X'$ with $T_{J\cup\{a\}}$; localization commutes with the displayed root-ring colimits. The supplied $\mathcal N|_{T_J}$ is lisse because restricting a finite-free local trivialization remains finite free. The coefficient criterion, applied separately to the actual $F=E$ or $F=\Omega$, gives the unit isomorphism
$$\mathcal N|_{T_J}[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}Re_*e^*\mathcal N|_{T_J}[0].$$
This step uses the norm-coefficient criterion as an unsplit analytical input; it does not deduce completeness of $\Omega$ or finite-field descent from step 4.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: apply the explicitly norm-topological coefficient criterion to the pro-etale base change and the supplied lisse module

proof.text:
For the closed immersion $d=d_{a,J}$ with complementary principal affine open $e$, [det-lem-formal-closed-support-adjunction] gives
$$R\underline\Gamma_{D_{a,J}}(\mathcal N|_{T_J}[0])\cong d^*\operatorname{fib}(\mathcal N|_{T_J}[0]\to Re_*e^*\mathcal N|_{T_J}[0]).$$
The actual unit on the right is an isomorphism by step 5, so its fibre and its exact inverse image are zero. This proves the asserted zero object in $D(D_{a,J},C_F)$. For an empty divisor $e$ is the identity and the same formula gives zero immediately; a rank-zero module is zero throughout. When $r=0$ no allowed $a,J$ exists, so the assertion is vacuous.
